script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The joke about walking past his own mustache in a mirror is hard to picture and does not make a clear comparison to recognizing someone.
The text does not say nobody was talking about anything else. It also does not establish as fact that Cleopas thought everyone must have heard.
Powerful in speech and action before God and all the people does not say Jesus spoke and acted in front of everyone.
The description of Jesus as powerful before God and all the people does not establish that He was not hiding.
Saying they told it as they lived it implies the two witnessed those events. The passage does not say that.
“I'll say it once and leave it right there” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The explanation repeats that redeem is the word without explaining the distinction or adding a meaningful insight.
The explanation repeatedly identifies the word but does not explain the hope the followers express.
The text says it is the third day, not that the two have been counting the days one by one.
The companions did not see Jesus. The text does not say He was not there.
The report says the companions did not see Jesus, not that nobody saw Him there.
The passage does not say the two had only seen the sadness of those days.
Calling Moses Israel's leader adds a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
The text says Jesus began with Moses and all the Prophets. It does not put the Prophets in a separate stage after Moses.
Calling David Israel's king adds a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Calling the burning hearts a good feeling assigns a feeling the text does not specify, without marking it as Papa's guess.
